questions.problem:
Which of the matrices below are singular?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
- For the matrix $A$, we have

$$
det(A)=0\cdot 0-1\cdot 1=-1.
$$

Because $det(A)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $A$ is invertible.

- The matrix $B$ is a $3\times 1$ matrix. So, it is not invertible. Since the matrix is not square, we can't say that it's singular.

- For the matrix $C$, we have

$$
det(C)=1\cdot 0-0\cdot 1=0.
$$

Because $det(C)=0,$ we conclude that $C$ is not invertible. Since $C$ is a square matrix that is not invertible, we also say that $C$ is singular.

Therefore, only $C$ is singular.

questions.problem: If $Q=[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ x & x\end{aligned}]$ is a singular matrix, calculate the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $Q$ is singular if and only if $det(Q)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Q) & =3\cdot x-x\cdot 6 \\  & =3x-6x \\  & =-3x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x & =0 \\ x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of $x$ is $x=0.$

questions.problem:
Which of the matrices below does **not** have an inverse?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 12 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
- The matrix $A$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix. So, it is not invertible.

- For the matrix $B$, we have

$$
det(B)=4\cdot (-1)-(-2)\cdot 3=2.
$$

Because $det(B)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $B$ is invertible.

- For the matrix $C$, we have

$$
det(C)=4\cdot 9-3\cdot 12=0.
$$

Because $det(C)=0,$ we conclude that $C$ is not invertible.

Therefore, only $A$ and $C$ do not have an inverse.

questions.problem:
If $B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3x+2 & 2x-4\end{aligned}]$
is a singular matrix, calculate the value of $x.$

$x=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $B$ is singular if and only if $det(B)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =1\cdot (2x-4)-2\cdot (3x+2) \\  & =2x-4-6x-4 \\  & =-4x-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-4x-8 & =0 \\ -4x & =8 \\ x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $B=[\begin{aligned}2x+4 & 0 \\ 15 & -x-3\end{aligned}]$
be a singular matrix. **In ascending order**, the values of $x$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}}$\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $B$ is singular if and only if $det(B)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =(2x+4)\cdot (-x-3)-0\cdot 15 \\  & =-2{x}^{2}-6x-4x-12 \\  & =-2{x}^{2}-10x-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}-10x-12 & =0 \\ -2({x}^{2}+5x+6) & =0 \\ (x+3)(x+2) & =0 \\ x & =-3,-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the values of $x$ are

$$
x=-3\,\text{and}\,x=-2.
$$
